svg.title: Example with made-up inputs: landed cost of three clothing orders
svg.desc: Example with made-up inputs. A US-made cotton T-shirt with a $35 value for duty sent by courier, an Asia-made jacket with a $120 value for duty shipped by courier from a US warehouse, and a US-made synthetic parka with a $300 value for duty. Each bar splits into item value, surtax at 50 percent of value for duty only when the goods are US-origin and the line is listed, customs duty, and GST at 5 percent of value for tax, which is $0 on the $35 row because that courier band is tax-free. Provincial sales tax is not shown.
svg.text: Example with made-up inputs: three courier orders
Bar length is Canadian dollars. GST is 5 percent, as in Customs Notice 26-23. Provincial tax is not shown.
Customs duty is $0 on all three rows
Surtax is 50 percent only on the two US-origin rows, and only if the line is on Schedule 3.
The jacket is not US-origin, so it has no surtax.
The $35 row is in the US courier band that is duty- and tax-free, so GST is $0. The surtax
still applies. Check with CBSA or your carrier. Duty is $0 through the courier band or UST Free.
Saving Optimizer. Example with made-up inputs. Checked 29 Sep 2026. Not a courier invoice.
